subject: chemistry
question_text: What is coefficient of viscosity? Give its units.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: The coefficient of viscosity η is the viscous
force between two liquid layers when the
velocity gradient between them and their area
From F = η A (du/dx): η = F when A = 1 and du/dx = 1
steps.why: The viscous force grows with the contact area and with how fast the speed changes between layers. Setting both to one isolates the constant η, which measures the liquid's own resistance to flow.
common_mistakes: Leaving out one of the two unit conditions. Both the velocity gradient and the area must be unity.
Calling η the friction between the liquid and the container wall. It acts between layers of the liquid itself.
steps.memory_tip: Two conditions set to one: unit area, unit velocity gradient. What is left of the force is η.
steps.margin_note: Writing F = ηA(du/dx) beside the words makes the definition exact.

steps.label: The units

lines.text: Units of η: N s m⁻² = Pa s

lines: CGS unit: poise (1 Pa s = 10 poise)
steps.why: Force (N) divided by area (m²) and by velocity gradient (s⁻¹) leaves N s m⁻². A pascal is one newton per square metre, so N s m⁻² is the same as Pa s.
common_mistakes: Writing N m⁻² without the s. That is pressure, not viscosity.
Writing Pa s⁻¹ instead of Pa s.
steps.memory_tip: Pressure times time: pascal second. The CGS cousin is the poise.
steps.margin_note: Either N s m⁻² or Pa s earns the mark; showing both is safest.

insider_note: The units carry a full mark of the two, and Pa s is the expected form — a correct definition with missing units drops half the question.
